title: Inference procurement decision tree & field validation sprint
creator: Asha Patel
description: Run a 2-week product research sprint to produce a practical decision tree that maps enterprise LLM buyers' procurement paths, the observable friction signals that trigger vendor substitution, and quantified fallback cost scenarios. Deliver an artifact (decision-tree + scoring sheet + short repo of SQL queries and dashboards) that Sales/Customer Success and Solutions Engineering can use to prioritize conversations and to surface early-warning signals in telemetry. Scope: enterprise buyers (finserv, healthtech), hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment choices, and switch-risk within the next 6 months.
problem_statement: Customers evaluate inference providers along latency, cost, SLA, model-compatibility, and procurement friction. We lack a concise, operational decision graph that ties product telemetry (latency spikes, quota hits), contract triggers, and buyer sentiment to the expected substitution probability and short-term revenue risk.
goals: Produce a decision tree artifact that maps 6 typical procurement checkpoints and 10 friction signals to recommended Redwood responses
Create a scoring sheet to estimate per-customer switch-risk (probability x ARR exposure) and fallback cost (latency delta, incremental token cost, operational lift)
Ship a small analytics workbook (SQL + dashboards) to detect the top 3 early-warning signals in our usage telemetry
Validate assumptions with 6 field interviews and 3 sales-facing workshops
acceptance_criteria: Decision tree (PNG + interactive Miro) uploaded to Confluence and shared with GTM
Scoring spreadsheet with example calculation for 5 anonymized customers
Dashboards: one real-time early-warning view and one historical cohort view (last 6 months)
At least 6 qualitative interviews logged (notes + snippet quotes) showing at least two common procurement pain points
Hand-off doc for Solutions Engineering with 3 recommended playbooks for low/medium/high switch-risk customers
updates: 2026-02-25 Asha: Ticket created. Draft plan and stakeholder list uploaded to Confluence. Tagged Sales, SE, Data Eng for collaboration.

2026-02-28 Marco: Ran initial cohort analysis. Identified 420 accounts with rising latency variance >20% and 73 accounts with billing-plan churn in last quarter. Saved SQL in repo: /analytics/pm/procurement_decision_tree.sql PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/analytics/pull/78

2026-03-03 Asha: Field interview guide drafted. Recruited 8 enterprise contacts via Solutions Engineering (consented 6). Miro decision-tree skeleton completed; link: https://miro.com/app/redwood/inference-procurement-tree
2026-03-07 Lina (Sales): Workshop feedback — procurement friction often tied to multi-region availability and contract SLAs, not just price. Added region-fallback branch to tree.

2026-03-10 Marco: Cost-sensitivity model prototype done. Modeled fallback cost for a mid-market search workload: +18% token cost and median latency increase of 120ms. Spreadsheet: https://drive.redwood.ai/sheets/procurement-sim-2026
2026-03-12 Asha: Ran 3 validation interviews. Key quote cataloged: 'We only consider switching if latency impact >200ms for customer-facing flows.' Adjusted scoring weights accordingly.
2026-03-14 Marco: Pulled telemetry dashboard into Console staging; can toggle 'procurement mode' to surface top-50 risk accounts. Preparing handoff doc to SEs for 2026-03-18 review.
stakeholders: Data Eng Team - owners of telemetry pipelines
risks_and_mitigations: Low interview volume: mitigation - compensate interviewees and extend window by 1 week
Telemetry signal noise: mitigation - run a small denoising pass and require signals to be persistent for 72 hours before flagging
Overfitting to high-ARR customers: mitigation - include 40% mid-market accounts in scoring sample

2026-03-16: SE handoff call to walk through playbooks and top-50 flagged accounts
